before.title: 10R60/10R80 MHT Harsh or Delayed Engagement and Shifts (TSB 22-2428)
before.description: Some 2020-2023 Lincoln Aviators equipped with a 10R60 and built on or before December 23, 2022, or a 10R80 MHT and built on or before August 15, 2022, may have harsh or delayed engagement and/or harsh or delayed shifts. Ford TSB 22-2428 says the condition may involve PCM/TCM software, the transmission solenoid-ID strategy, sticking main-control valves, or axial movement of the CDF clutch-cylinder sleeve. The complaint may occur with or without a malfunction indicator and the bulletin's listed transmission DTCs. The symptom alone does not select a valve body, CDF cylinder, or complete transmission.
before.solution: Have a Ford/Lincoln-capable technician confirm the transmission and build date, retrieve PCM/TCM faults, and follow TSB 22-2428 in order. The bulletin begins with available PCM/TCM programming and an adaptive-learning drive cycle, then uses the stored faults and clutch behavior to select an accelerated main-control break-in routine. If the condition remains, the procedure can require main-control overhaul and, only after the bulletin's later tests fail, condition-specific internal transmission repair. Parts and coverage must be selected by VIN and the actual failed step; this record intentionally has no buy link.

before.title: Aviator Transmission Safety Recalls: Park and Direction-Control Defects
before.description: Three separate VIN-scoped transmission recalls affect limited Aviator populations. NHTSA 26V402 covers certain 2020-2021 vehicles whose separator-plate design can restrict flow to the park valve, allow temporary park-pawl engagement while moving, damage the park system, and create a later rollaway risk. NHTSA 23V070/Ford 23S06 covers certain 2023 Aviators whose transmission may contain a loose extra bolt that can block the park pawl even when the selector shows Park. NHTSA 25V164/Ford 25S19 covers specified 2025 Aviators built December 4-20, 2024, whose main-control valve body may cause no reverse or unexpected forward motion in Reverse or Neutral. These campaigns are not interchangeable and do not cover every listed model year.
before.solution: Check the VIN in the NHTSA and Lincoln/Ford recall systems and follow the instructions for the campaign actually open. For 26V402, follow the current do-not-drive advisory and contact a Lincoln dealer for transport guidance; the free remedy is updated PCM software plus inspection and replacement of damaged park-system components as needed. For 23S06, the dealer inspects for the loose bolt and replaces the transmission if the inspection fails. For 25S19, the dealer replaces the transmission main-control valve body. Do not buy transmission parts or combine a harsh-shift complaint with these recall remedies without VIN confirmation.
symptoms: Vehicle movement after Park when the park system has been damaged on a 26V402-covered vehicle
Selector shows Park but the park pawl does not engage on a 23V070-covered vehicle
No reverse motion on a 25V164-covered vehicle
Unexpected forward motion with Reverse or Neutral selected on a 25V164-covered vehicle

before.title: 12-Volt Battery Drain from Third-Party App Modem Activity
before.description: Ford SSM 50804 says some 2020-2022 Aviators with an activated modem may have 12-volt battery-drain symptoms when unaffiliated third-party phone applications repeatedly request vehicle commands such as lock, unlock, remote start, or location. Those calls can keep the vehicle network active. This is one documented cause, not proof that every dead battery is a TCU, latch, battery, or module failure. Ford separately explains that a Deep Sleep notification can be normal after 14 days, low voltage, state of charge below 50 percent, or a TCU update.
before.solution: Identify and uninstall any non-Ford/Lincoln app that accesses the vehicle, then fully charge and test the 12-volt battery and monitor key-off draw and battery state of charge. If symptoms remain, follow normal Ford battery, battery-monitoring-sensor, charging-system, modem, and module network-sleep diagnostics. A Deep Sleep notification by itself is not a failed module; if state of charge does not change after charging or a BMS reset, continue the battery/BMS diagnostic path. Do not replace a latch, TCU, battery, or other module without a failed test, and do not present a maintainer as the repair for an unresolved drain.
symptoms: 12-volt battery discharges while the vehicle is parked
No-start or low-voltage condition
Repeated modem activity associated with a third-party vehicle-control app
Deep Sleep notification requiring state-of-charge evaluation if it persists after charging
affectedSystems: vehicle modem and telematics control unit

Ford SSM 50975: Deep Sleep Mode Notification and Battery/BMS Diagnosis

before.title: 3.0L EcoBoost Intake-Valve Fracture Recall 24S55 / NHTSA 24V635
before.description: Certain 2021-2022 Lincoln Aviators with 3.0-liter Nano EcoBoost engines are included in Ford recall 24S55/NHTSA 24V635. Intake valves produced outside the intended hardness specification can fracture while driving, causing engine failure and loss of drive power. Ford's later customer-satisfaction program identifies Aviator engine/build ranges from June through October 2021 and provides additional long-block coverage after the recall inspection. Inclusion is VIN-specific; the 2.7-liter engine named in the multi-model recall does not describe an Aviator powertrain.
before.solution: Check the VIN and have a Ford/Lincoln dealer complete recall 24S55. The free recall remedy is an engine-cycle inspection test; the dealer replaces the engine only when the procedure determines replacement is necessary. Vehicles that completed the inspection process may qualify for the no-cost, one-time long-block program under CSP 24N12 for 10 years or 150,000 miles from warranty start, subject to its terms. Do not buy a long block or internal-engine parts for this recall. If the engine loses power or develops a severe running problem, move out of traffic safely and contact Lincoln for service guidance.
symptoms: Sudden loss of drive power if an intake valve fractures
Engine failure
Severe rough running or misfire if the failure occurs

before.title: Air-Suspension Fault B1041/U2100 After SUMA Diagnostic Service Mode
before.description: Some 2020-2023 Aviators equipped with air suspension may display a Drive Malfunction and/or Suspension Fault message with DTCs B1041 and U2100 stored in Suspension Control Module A (SUMA). Ford SSM 51621 says this bulletin-defined condition can occur when SUMA enters diagnostic service mode after an on-demand self-test following suspension diagnosis or repair. It does not identify a leaking air spring, compressor, height sensor, or solenoid as the cause of these two codes.
before.solution: Use Ford Diagnosis and Repair System (FDRS) and select SUMA > Run All CM (Continuous Memory) DTCs. Do not run SUMA > OD and CM DTCs for this condition because the on-demand self-test can create the invalid codes. If that test was run, clear the condition with SUMA > Transport and Factory Mode Deactivation. If other DTCs or physical ride-height symptoms remain, follow Workshop Manual Section 204-05 normal diagnostics before selecting a part. This record intentionally has no commerce link.

before.title: Battery-Cable Harness Contact with A/C Pulley - Recall 21S34 / 21V534
before.description: Certain 2020-2021 Lincoln Aviators with the 3.0-liter gasoline engine are included in Ford recall 21S34/NHTSA 21V534. An improperly secured battery-cable wire harness can contact the A/C compressor pulley. Continued rubbing may damage the harness insulation or drive belt and expose the unfused positive battery circuit, creating a short-circuit and fire risk. Inclusion is determined by VIN rather than model year alone.
before.solution: Check the VIN and arrange the free recall remedy with a Lincoln dealer. The dealer installs a tie strap to keep the harness away from the A/C compressor pulley and inspects the harness for contact damage, repairing or replacing it as necessary. Do not purchase a generic harness, belt, or compressor part for the campaign. If smoke, burning odor, or an electrical short is present, stop safely, shut the vehicle down away from structures when possible, and contact emergency or Lincoln service assistance as appropriate.

Visible battery-cable harness contact or insulation damage near the A/C compressor pulley
Smoke, burning odor, or electrical short if damage progresses

before.title: PHEV P1A0C and Stop Safely Now After Remote-Start/Charge-Cord Sequence - CSP 22P16
before.description: Certain 2020-2022 Aviator PHEVs are included in Ford Customer Satisfaction Program 22P16. For a matching SSM 49914 or 49015 software condition, use the latest Ford diagnostic software to reprogram the RGTM. If the symptom does not match, continue Workshop Manual diagnosis of power, grounds, switches, latch, position sensing, struts, wiring, and obstruction detection before selecting a part. This record intentionally has no commerce link.

Power liftgate is inoperative
Early-build liftgate opens only partially
False anti-theft alarm with liftgate-ajar sensing

before.title: Lack of Audio with Rear-Liftgate or Spare-Tire Water Leak - TSB 23-2181
before.description: Some 2020-2023 Aviators may exhibit lack of audio after rainfall or a car wash together with water in the rear-liftgate area or spare-tire area. Ford TSB 23-2181 directs Aviator-specific inspection of the power-liftgate grommet, margin seal and pushpins, electrical-wiring grommet, rear washer hose, body-hole plugs, BLIS-module seating, and BLIS harness grommets. before.solution: Confirm both the audio symptom and rear water evidence, then follow the Aviator inspection sequence in TSB 23-2181. If right-side water is present, follow the bulletin's ACM replacement step and use the VIN-specific parts catalog application. Dry and inspect affected connectors and trim as directed. Coverage depends on the vehicle's applicable warranty or service plan; this record has no commerce link.

before.title: Unexpected Acceleration and Phantom Braking With Driver-Assist (Co-Pilot360 / BlueCruise) Engaged
before.description: Owners across multiple model years report two opposite but related ADAS misbehaviors. With adaptive cruise / driver-assist (Co-Pilot360, ActiveGlide/BlueCruise) engaged, the Aviator has unexpectedly ACCELERATED toward a stopped vehicle instead of continuing to slow, and separately has applied PHANTOM BRAKING — abrupt, unprompted automatic braking triggered by harmless objects such as a crack in the driveway, overpass shadows, or roadside features. Some events come with 'Antilock brake fault' or 'Pre-Collision Assist not available' messages. These are hard to reproduce on demand and are documented in NHTSA complaints and owner forums; no broad recall specifically targets this behavior.
before.solution: Report any unexpected-acceleration or phantom-braking event to NHTSA (vehicle safety hotline / nhtsa.gov) and to the dealer, with date/time so the module can be scanned for stored events. Ensure all camera/radar sensors are clean, undamaged, and properly aimed (especially after any windshield or bumper work, which requires ADAS recalibration), and that the IPMA/ADAS modules are on the latest software (see related camera/IPMA recalls). Until resolved, use driver-assist features cautiously and keep ready to override with throttle/brake; treat repeated events as a safety concern warranting dealer investigation.
symptoms: Vehicle accelerates toward a stopped car while adaptive cruise/driver-assist is on
Sudden hard automatic braking for no real obstacle (phantom braking)
Abrupt stops triggered by pavement cracks, shadows, or overpasses
'Pre-Collision Assist not available' or 'Antilock brake fault' messages
Driver-assist disengages unexpectedly during the event

proposal.title: Unexpected Acceleration and Phantom Braking With Driver-Assist (Co-Pilot360 / BlueCruise) Engaged
proposal.description: The NHTSA complaints API contains individual Aviator allegations, not proof of one common defect. ODI 11644108 alleges a 2021 vehicle changed its cruise set speed upward; ODI 11554066 alleges automatic braking with no nearby obstacle; ODI 11623452 alleges a 2022 vehicle accelerated from Park while pre-collision braking did not engage; ODI 11734097 alleges 2025 cruise acceleration/deceleration and false crash warnings; and ODI 11677763 alleges automatic braking with ABS and pre-collision faults. These reports describe different events and do not establish one Co-Pilot360/BlueCruise cause, a failure across every indexed year or engine, or a repair. The exact API replay found no matching 2024 complaint under the audit’s acceleration/braking/driver-assistance terms.
proposal.solution: If the vehicle accelerates or brakes unexpectedly, take control, disengage driver assistance when it can be done safely, and stop in a safe location if warnings or control problems persist. Preserve the date, time, road, speed, selected assistance mode, warnings, weather and full diagnostic scan; report the event to Lincoln and NHTSA. Have camera, radar, braking, powertrain and driver-assistance systems diagnosed against the exact event and stored data. Do not promise sensor cleaning, calibration, module software, a brake repair, or any replacement part without a matching fault and Ford procedure. No universal sensor, camera, radar, module, brake component, software update or retail part is asserted.
